BiblicalUsage: Gazzah is a fleece, and it belongs to Gideon's test. He put a fleece of wool in the floor in Judges 6:37, and if the dew was on the fleece only, he would know God would save Israel by his hand. It was so, and he wrung a bowl full of water from the fleece in Judges 6:38. Then he asked once more, in Judges 6:39, that the fleece be dry and the ground wet, and God did so that night in Judges 6:40.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Gideon's fleece shows a fearful man asking God to be patient with him. God answered twice, wet and dry, and I hold that He bears with our testing when our hearts are honestly seeking His will.
